adf.name: Azure Data Factory
adf.summary: Pay-as-you-go meters for activity runs, copy time and data flow compute.
adf.bestWhen: You live on Azure, run pipelines a few times a day, have SSIS packages, or must reach on-premises databases through a self-hosted runtime.
adf.watchOut: Very frequent runs add up fast, and the bill is hard to forecast without a trial.

fabric.name: Fabric Data Factory
fabric.summary: Microsoft's next generation of Data Factory, billed in capacity units.
fabric.bestWhen: You are already buying Fabric capacity.
fabric.watchOut: It is billed differently, and the page we read lists no per-unit dollar rate.

perrow.name: Per-row or credit-based tools
perrow.summary: Tools such as Fivetran and Airbyte bill on a different unit, such as changed rows or credits.
perrow.bestWhen: You want a bill tied to rows or credits instead of copy time and cluster time.
perrow.watchOut: Your forecast depends on that unit, so check how it counts your data.

glue.name: AWS Glue
glue.bestWhen: Your team already lives on AWS.
glue.watchOut: This post does not break down Glue's meters, so check its pricing before you decide.

informatica.name: Informatica
